title: Heat and Thermodynamics
description: The heat and thermodynamics course (Basic Principles of Physics, BMAS): temperature and thermometry, thermal expansion, heat capacity and latent heat, conduction, convection and radiation, kinetic theory and ideal gases, the first law and thermodynamic processes, and heat engines, refrigerators, the second law and entropy. Built from the PHY 103 slides of Dr E. Oyeniyi and Mr A. O. Ayoola and the heat engine, Carnot, conduction and radiation slides, with the 2010/11 PHY 115 paper and a typed PHY 103 exam.

topics.title: Temperature and Thermometry
topics.summary: Temperature tells whether bodies are in thermal equilibrium, and the zeroth law makes thermometers possible. Thermometers use properties that change with temperature, calibrated on the Kelvin, Celsius and Fahrenheit scales.
subtopics: Heat, thermal contact and thermal equilibrium
Thermometric properties and types of thermometer
The Kelvin scale, triple point and absolute zero
Linear temperature scales from fixed points

topics.title: Thermal Expansion
topics.summary: Most materials expand when heated. Linear, area and volume expansivities describe the change, and preventing expansion produces large thermal stresses.
subtopics: Expansion of holes and hollow bodies

topics.title: Heat Capacity, Latent Heat and Calorimetry
topics.summary: Heat raises temperature according to the specific heat capacity and changes state according to the latent heat. Calorimetry balances heat lost and gained in mixtures.
subtopics: Heat capacity and specific heat capacity
Latent heat of fusion and vaporisation

topics.title: Heat Transfer: Conduction, Convection and Radiation
topics.summary: Heat travels by conduction through matter, by convection in fluids and by radiation through empty space. Fourier's law and the Stefan–Boltzmann law make conduction and radiation quantitative.

topics.title: Kinetic Theory and Ideal Gases
topics.summary: The ideal gas law relates pressure, volume, temperature and amount of gas. Kinetic theory explains pressure by molecular impacts and links the average kinetic energy of molecules to absolute temperature.
subtopics: Gas laws and the ideal gas equation
Moles, molar mass and Avogadro's number

topics.title: The First Law and Thermodynamic Processes
topics.summary: The first law states that heat supplied equals the rise in internal energy plus the work done by the system. Isothermal, adiabatic, isobaric, isochoric and cyclic processes each apply it differently, and work is the area under the P–V curve.
subtopics: The first law: Q = ΔU + W
Work done as the area under a P–V curve

topics.title: Heat Engines, the Second Law and Entropy
topics.summary: A heat engine takes heat from a hot reservoir, does work and rejects heat to a cold reservoir; a refrigerator reverses this. The Carnot cycle sets the upper limit on efficiency, the second law forbids perfect engines, and entropy measures the direction of natural processes.
subtopics: The Carnot cycle and Carnot efficiency
Reversible and irreversible processes; the third law
